summary: Agent skill that turns a technical book or folder of documents into a reusable skill your coding agent can study and look things up in.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: book-to-skill converts a technical book, a document folder or a collection of sources into one agent skill. Your coding agent can then study, reference and use that material while you work, in tools like Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI and Amp.
sixtySeconds.problem: Pasting a whole book into an agent's context is slow and expensive. The README says its generated skill answers a question with 24 to 51 times fewer tokens than dumping the book in.
whoFor: Developers who learn from technical books
Teams turning internal docs into agent knowledge
Coding agent users across many tools
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to give your agent a compact, searchable version of the books and docs you rely on, installable in many agent hosts.
requirements: A coding agent that supports skills (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Amp and others)
Node.js for npx, or Git for manual install

overview: Install with the cross-agent skills CLI (npx skills add) or clone it into your agent's skills folder, for example ~/.claude/skills/book-to-skill for Claude Code.

Run /book-to-skill with local files (PDF, EPUB, DOCX, Markdown and more) and an optional skill name, or /book-to-skill search to discover and read sources through MCP. The skill is created in ~/.agents/skills/<slug>/.
There are also analyse-only, generate-from-analysis and update workflows, and it can publish the generated skill to GitHub, private by default. The project is MIT licensed.
